title: Rudolf Blaschka 1892 — shipment, production-lane and expedition-output crosswalk
research_question: How do the 1892 journey, stationary Hosterwitz production, later model-making and outbound shipments relate when shipment is treated as an aggregation event rather than a production-time unit?
current_thesis: 1892 split the workshop without stopping production. One maker travelled while Leopold continued manufacturing at Hosterwitz; reference packets and finished models moved asynchronously; later shipments serially aggregated work with different production dates, makers and reference genealogies.
analytical_terms_guard: split workshop, packet, aggregation technology, serial reassembly and production queue are project analytical terms, not actor vocabulary unless independently attested.

stationary_production_lane.journey_side_corroboration: BLA-D00884-00885: Rudolf responds to his father's report about work while in Colorado
stationary_production_lane.shipment_queue: These models enter the seventh shipment in February 1893, months after production.
stationary_production_lane.analytical_value: Production clock and shipment clock diverge; the workshop remains active at Hosterwitz while Rudolf travels.

field_media_decisions.event: Ganong handles plants in glass containers with alcohol and water and as dried specimens; two boxes of material already sent to Cambridge to stay until Rudolf is ready to return.
Rudolf says cacti are better received alive than in alcohol because the workshop can grow the flower itself; three cacti were collected in Jamaica.
field_media_decisions.mechanism: transport medium preserves different future epistemic affordances

field_media_decisions.event: after completing 36 species in San Diego, Rudolf sends a small box of cacti and flowering bulbs with other things to Cambridge for Goodale to forward to Hosterwitz; a giant-cactus cutting may rot.
field_media_decisions.mechanism: live transport + viability risk + relay through Harvard

field_media_decisions.event: Crinum bulb and earlier seed packet arrive from Orcutt after the party has left California; Rudolf plans continued seed/bulb supply for flowering windows the journey could not wait for.
field_media_decisions.mechanism: seasonal delay converted into future-supply relation

production_afterlife.claim: Rudolf estimates drawing/studying/collecting has produced about three years of material.
37 ordinary plant models explicitly partitioned as 20 Jamaica, 15 West, 2 garden, plus a scientific second portion.
planned 50-species consignment described as almost entirely based on Jamaica/West material and studies.
workshop still preparing American-collected plants; some material takes weeks; many Arizona/California forms lacked pictures in books.
